Definition: the trunk or stump of a tree (as felled or as planted)
BiblicalUsage: gezaʻ — stem, trunk, stock (of trees). That is the whole of it, and it is enough: 3 occurrences, and in Job and Isaiah the meaning never wavers. I keep coming back to the simple reading because the simple reading is the true one.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe gezaʻ matters because God speaks plainly, and plain words carry real weight. I hold that the simple reading is the true one, and I will not trade it for a clever one.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
